course_description:
This course provides tools and critical perspectives for the analysis, development and use of curriculum materials in second language classrooms. It provides students with an overview of dominant and emergent approaches to the teaching of TESOL, hands-on review of instructional materials, and classroom instructional techniques and strategies. This course may not be offered in person if the enrolment is less than 10 students.

Thisﾠcourse uses applied principles of second language acquisition (SLA), with specific reference to practical classroom strategies for the learning and teaching of English to Speakers of other languages (TESOL). It provides a meta-language for discussing SLA and focuses on pedagogical strategies which teachers can use in a range of educational settings. The pedagogy of language teaching is approached via understandings about communicative competence and more recent concepts that refer to the kind of language ability that is needed for communication in a globalised world. Language teaching is explored through the macro planning of curriculum design and at the micro level of the classroom lesson. The development of the macro-skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing are surveyed as embedded within the social context of language learning. Reflection on context and previous experience is emphasised. Students should take away from this course ideas that work in classrooms and ‘theories’ about why this is the case. Learning achievement in the course is assessed by curriculum design, micro teaching and critical reflection as students of teaching.

restrictions: Restricted to students enrolled in the GCEdSt, MEdSt, GCAppLing or MAppLing. In Person offering may be cancelled unless a minimum of 10 students enrol.
Another instance of the same course
Each week there is a one-hour hybrid (simultaneous face-to-face and zoom) lecture for both In Person and Externally enrolled students.

Additional timetable information
This course is being offered in internal and external modes concurrently. The 2-hour weekly tutorial is to be attended face-to-face by internal students and online (zoom) by external students.
Students are expected to attend both the lectures and the interactive tutorials, as these provide valuable learning opportunities and experiences.
course_aims: The course aims to enrich studentsﾒ repertoire of classroom techniques and strategies for teaching and learning of English to speakers of other languages by enhancing their understanding of how second languages are learned on the one hand and engaging them in the design, evaluation and reflection of classroom instruction andﾠinstructional materials in the light of contemporary L2 pedagogy on the other.

learning_outcomes.description: select, adopt and create materials and resources relevant for your teaching context
critically evaluate your readings and other material presented
review, analyse and critique materials related to TESOL curriculum and instruction
engage in reflective practice related to your own teaching and that of others
apply your understanding of how second languages are learned to language program design and instruction

assessment_details.title: Curriculum Design
assessment_details.task_description: This curriculum design project entails the preparation of a unit of work, or mini curriculum, applying the curriculum design model, proposed by Macalister and Nation (2020). In this project you will design, develop, teach (imagine) and justify a segment of a TESOL program or syllabus for a group of students for whom you are or might be responsible. Your unit design should consist of at least 3 lessons but should not exceed 5 lessons in total . Programs may be based on classes you have taught recently or classes that could be taught in EFL contexts, ELICOS, Migrant Education, schools (Pre, Primary, Secondary), or classes you’d like to teach, etc. either in Australia or overseas. In designing your curriculum, you should address the following: Part A. The environment for your course, considering the nature of the learners, the teachers and the teaching situation The learner group and their specific language learning needs. The principles of language teaching and learning used to guide your design. Part B. The goals of your unit Summary content and sequencing of a series of lessons Materials used for learning Assessment of learning, both formative and summative Part C. Reflective justification of your design, drawing clear connections between part A and Part B. In this section you should argue the relevance of your curriculum design for the teaching situation and the needs of the learner group. The choices that you make in relation to goals, content, materials and assessment processes should be clearly justified in relation to research-informed theories of language teaching and learning. You should draw on course readings and current relevant literature to support your justification. Note that your curriculum design project should not be based on an existing English language course book . Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.task_description: This assessment comprises two components: (1) an interactive oral micro-teaching presentation and (2) a Q&A session. Students must pass both components to successfully complete this assessment. For the micro-teaching presentation, students will deliver an interactive lesson based on aspect(s) of the topics covered in the course that they selected for their curriculum design (Assessment 2) with help of required resources such as ppt slides. They will enact the teaching plan developed for their mini curriculum. This task is designed to reflect authentic teaching practice, as teaching will be a central responsibility in students’ future TESOL careers. Peers enrolled in the course will take on the role of students, providing an opportunity to engage in the lesson activities and learn from one another’s presentations. Each presentation will run for 15 minutes and will be followed by a 5 to 7-minute Q&A session with peers and the lecturer/tutor. Presentations will be conducted in tutorial groups, either face-to-face or via Zoom. As part of their participation, students are required to ask at least one constructive question during a classmate’s presentation. Active engagement as an audience member will also contribute to the overall mark. If you use AI and/or machine translation (MT) tools in preparing your presentation resources such as ppt slides, script and notes, you must provide clear and specific details about how they were used. Failure to acknowledge the use of generative AI or MT may constitute academic misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Guidelines on appropriate referencing and acknowledgement, including an example coversheet, are available here: Overview - AI tools for assignments - Library Guides at University of Queensland Library The Q&A component is designed to uphold academic integrity and assess your understanding of relevant TESOL concepts. You are expected to ask questions following peers’ presentations and respond to questions about your own presentation spontaneously, without the use of AI tools or other materials such as slides or scripts. The use of these prohibited materials during the Q&A session may be investigated and treated as academic misconduct. Please note that questions posed to peers must be spontaneous and not pre-prepared. Students will have to pass both micro-teaching presentation and Q&A components to pass this assessment task. Micro-teaching presentations will commence in Week 10. The presentation schedule will be made available to students by Week 8. Read full task description Hide full task description
